deep.reconstruction:
Context. The previous page (fol. 144r) sets up a surface T spread simply or multiply over the (x,y)-plane, i.e. a Riemann surface. It introduces functions X, Y on T with X dx + Y dy an exact differential (dX/dy - dY/dx = 0), and cross-cuts (Querschnitte) that make T simply connected. This is the draft of Part I of Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857). Section 2 of that paper treats analysis situs and integrals of exact differentials. Section 3 is titled 'Bestimmung einer Function einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse durch Grenz- und Unstetigkeitsbedingungen', and that exact heading appears on this page. The page drafts the Dirichlet-principle argument of section 3, which goes back to Dissertation 1851, sections 16-18.

(1) Top lines, partly struck. For the integral D(alpha) = ∫_T (alpha_x^2 + alpha_y^2) dT, the first variation, alpha -> alpha + eps*lambda, is
2∫(alpha_x lambda_x + alpha_y lambda_y) dT = 2∮ lambda (d alpha/dn) ds - 2∫ lambda Δalpha dT.
So for harmonic alpha it depends only on the variation at the boundary. It vanishes when the variation is zero there. [Integration by parts supplied by me.]

(2) The real object is Riemann's functional
Omega(alpha) = ∫_T [ (alpha_x - beta_y)^2 + (alpha_y + beta_x)^2 ] dT,
where alpha + i*beta is a given comparison function carrying the prescribed boundary and discontinuity behaviour. Omega measures the failure of the Cauchy-Riemann equations. One minimizes over alpha, with beta fixed (or alpha replaced by alpha + lambda, lambda vanishing on the boundary). [Implicit step, mine:] the first variation is
-2∫ lambda (Δalpha - beta_yx + beta_xy) dT = -2∫ lambda Δalpha dT,
so the minimizer u is harmonic.

(3) Construction of the conjugate. Write v = beta + nu, so that u + i v is to be analytic. The Cauchy-Riemann equations v_x = -u_y, v_y = u_x give
dnu = d(v - beta) = -(alpha_y + beta_x) dx + (alpha_x - beta_y) dy,
with alpha standing for the minimizer. This is the final line 'nu - beta = V = ...'.
- The integrability condition is d/dy[-(alpha_y + beta_x)] = d/dx[alpha_x - beta_y]. The beta terms cancel, leaving exactly Δalpha = 0, which is precisely the Euler-Lagrange equation of Omega. [Remark mine.]
- The first attempt 'V = (alpha_x + beta_y) dy + (alpha_y + beta_x) dx' has wrong signs. So do the struck intermediate attempts. They were corrected in the final line.
- The struck lines 'v = beta + nu', 'u = alpha + mu', 'du/dx = ...' are notational trials for splitting the solution into given part plus correction.

(4) Heading 'Ueber die Bestimmung einer Function einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse durch Grenz- und Unstetigkeitsbedingungen'. Below it are heavily struck attempts at a motivating sentence: 'Aus diesem Grunde ist hier eine besondere Darstellung ... nöthig'. These are followed by a classification of discontinuities. Functions for which nu (the conjugate) stays finite independently of (alpha - lambda) are called discontinuous of the first kind. Those where this is not so (nu acquires infinities or periods) are called discontinuous of the second kind. This anticipates the distinction in section 3 of the 1857 paper between discontinuities whose conjugate is single-valued and logarithmic-type ones.
errors: First expression for V, '(alpha_x + beta_y) dy + (alpha_y + beta_x) dx', has sign errors. Correct is -(alpha_y + beta_x) dx + (alpha_x - beta_y) dy, as in Riemann's own final line.
Struck line 'du/dx = dalpha/dx + dbeta/dx' is a slip (should be dalpha/dx + dmu/dx if u = alpha + mu). It was deleted by Riemann.
The claim that the first variation depends only on boundary values presupposes Δalpha = 0 (or is meant at the extremal). This is standard, not an error, but unstated.

results.what: First variation of the Dirichlet integral reduces to a boundary term; vanishes for variations zero on the boundary
results.modern_name: Euler-Lagrange equation for the Dirichlet energy / Dirichlet principle
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Thomson (Kelvin) 1847, Dirichlet (lectures); named by Riemann

results.what: Minimization of Omega = ∫((alpha_x - beta_y)^2 + (alpha_y + beta_x)^2) dT to produce an analytic function with prescribed boundary/discontinuity behaviour
results.modern_name: Riemann's Dirichlet-principle existence proof for analytic functions/abelian integrals on Riemann surfaces

results.what: Conjugate function nu - beta = ∫[-(alpha_y + beta_x) dx + (alpha_x - beta_y) dy], exact iff alpha harmonic
results.usually_credited_to: Cauchy/Riemann; this exact form is in Riemann's dissertation

results.what: Classification of discontinuities into first and second kind according to behaviour of the conjugate function
results.modern_name: Types of singularities of abelian integrals / harmonic functions (poles vs logarithmic singularities with periods)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of section 3 of Riemann's published 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (1857), with the heading verbatim. The functional and conjugate construction appear identically in his 1851 dissertation. It is of interest only as a record of drafting (sign corrections, wording of the discontinuity classification).

transcription_corrections: Line 'V = (dα/dx + dβ/dy) dy + (dα/dy + dβ/dx) dx' in the image reads with the dy term first and is an uncorrected first attempt (wrong signs), not the final result.
'tt' in the last paragraph is most likely 'ff' (Riemann's abbreviation for 'Functionen'): 'die Abweichung ... bei den ff, in welchen ν unabhängig der Endlichkeit von (α−λ) ...'.
'Abhängigkeit' in the last paragraphs is uncertain; possibly 'Abweichung'.
The struck marginal lines read 'v = β + ν' and 'u = α + μ' (left margin), as transcribed. 'ν − β = V' on the final formula line is correctly read.
The heading should read 'Ueber die Bestimmung einer Function einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse durch Grenz- und Unstetigkeitsbedingungen' (matching the 1857 section 3 title).
